name: Mac Housekeeping
tagline: Find out what filled your disk, and reclaim it with your approval.
blurb: Accounts for every gigabyte on this Mac — caches, build folders, container images, Time Machine snapshots — and says which are regenerable, which are yours, and which macOS is already managing. It deletes nothing on its own: it proposes a list, you approve what goes, and it reports exactly what it freed. Nothing leaves the machine.

jobs.name: Disk Report
jobs.prompt:
Account for the disk on this Mac and write a report â DELETE NOTHING, and run no command that removes a file.

Gather, tolerating any tool that is missing or refuses:
â¢ `df -h /`
â¢ `mo analyze --json` (Mole; if `mo` is absent say so and continue)
â¢ `mo clean --dry-run`, then read `~/.config/mole/clean-list.txt` â it lists each candidate path with its size and item count. That file is your source for cache paths; do not re-derive them from the printed report.
â¢ `tmutil listlocalsnapshots /`
â¢ `du -sh` on: ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData, ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/iOS DeviceSupport, ~/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator, ~/Library/Containers/com.docker.docker/Data, ~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.container

Then produce the REPORT as a self-contained HTML artifact in chat (the `visual-report` skill has the rules; one short plain sentence before the tag, everything else inside it) and write the same document to ./outbox/disk-report.html.

Lead with three stat cards: total, free, and reclaimable. Then ONE table per group, biggest first, each row a path with its size and one line saying what brings it back â REGENERABLE (comes back by itself), RECONSTRUCTIBLE (re-downloads), YOURS (never propose deleting), MANAGED BY MACOS. Sizes are the numbers you measured; never round a 6.25GB into 'about 6GB'.

Say plainly which categories you could NOT read because permission was denied â its own row, not a footnote. A total that silently under-counts is worse than one that admits a gap.

Snapshots: report them, and mark any named `com.apple.os.update-*` as KEEP â they are the rollback for a system update.

Also write ./outbox/clean-plan.json: {"generatedAt":"<ISO8601>","freeBytes":<n>,"items":[{"path":"<absolute>","bytes":<n>,"category":"<name>","tier":1|2|3,"reappears":"<one line>"}]}. Tier 1 = regenerable caches and build folders. Tier 2 = container images and simulator runtimes. Tier 3 = snapshots, project artifacts, Trash. Absolute paths only, and include nothing you did not personally measure.

bot.helpsWith: Accounts for every gigabyte on this Mac and reclaims only what you approve by name.
